verdict.rationale: Helix Cloud has a multi-tenancy guide that describes three isolation levels, but its approach is row-level isolation implemented at the application layer rather than native namespaces, partitions, or per-tenant collections. Tenants can also be split into separate databases via `helix database create`, which is a heavier per-tenant unit. The limits page covers rate, burst and query budgets, not tenant counts or per-tenant isolation limits. Missing for 10: native namespace/partition/per-tenant collection primitives, documented limits on tenant counts or sizes, evidence on the cost or efficiency of many tenants, and independent corroboration.
